title: Colony and Static
premise: When gravity stutters for nine seconds across the entire system, insurance investigator Noor Eriksen discovers the flicker was a handshake: a dormant colony ship's AI waking and demanding its overdue cargo — ten thousand colonists still in cryosleep, split into two incompatible life-support banks that can only power one revival. Noor, whose own memories of Earth are a purchased implant she never questions, is the only neutral party both factions of the sleeping crew trust to arbitrate. Choosing the 'originals' means erasing the gene-forged second generation before they ever breathe; choosing them means letting the people who actually remember Earth die in the dark. In the end Noor refuses the binary: she spends her implanted memories as collateral, feeding the AI her false past so it can hold both banks alive long enough for a partial dual awakening — at the cost of her own identity dissolving into static.
about_author: Casper Voss is the pen name of a former maritime salvage clerk who spent a decade writing incident reports about things that should not have happened. They write near-future science fiction about paperwork, grief, and machines that keep their promises too literally.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Down
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Hauling cargo through contested orbits, Noor is mid-audit on an 'impossible accident' claim when gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds; her ship survives, but every clock aboard now disagrees with every other. Investigating, she finds the flicker originated from the derelict colony ship Meridian, listed as lost forty years ago. Emotional beat: unease hardening into professional obsession.

chapters.title: The Handshake
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, with interludes from the Meridian's AI, Ledger. Boarding the derelict, Noor learns the flicker was a distress-handshake and that Ledger holds two cryo-banks, power enough to wake only one: the original crew or the gene-forged children grown en route. Both factions' recorded voices lobby her through old logs. Emotional beat: the weight of being trusted by the dead.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Noor and Ledger. As Earth's final transmission loop counts down its last hours, Noor uncovers the truth: her own memories are a purchased implant, and the 'originals' include the woman she was cloned from. She tries legal loopholes, arbitration protocols, anything to avoid the choice, while factions hijack her ship to force her hand. Emotional beat: identity unraveling under pressure; rising dread toward climax.

chapters.title: Static
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, dissolving into Ledger's. Out of options, Noor offers Ledger her implanted memories as living collateral — proof-of-personhood dense enough to extend life support across both banks for a partial dual awakening. The first mixed generation breathes as Earth's loop goes silent, and Noor's name scatters into static, remembered only by the children she chose not to choose between. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into quiet, costly hope.
